Section 4: Leave and Absence

This section explains how much leave you are entitled to, how to request it and what happens when you are unable to work. It applies to all employees, whether full time or part time, from the first day of employment.
4.1 Annual leave
Entitlement
Your entitlement depends on your length of service on 1 January of the leave year. Part-time employees receive a pro-rata entitlement.
Length of serviceDays per yearMaximum carry-overLess than 2 years255 days2 to 4 years275 days5 to 9 years297 days10 years or more3110 days
How to request leave
Leave must be approved by your line manager before it is booked. Requests are made through the HR portal at least two weeks ahead. You can also use the command line tool:
hr-portal submit --form L-12 --from 2026-08-03 --to 2026-08-07
A request is approved only when you receive a confirmation e-mail. The following rules apply to all requests:
(a) No more than ten consecutive working days may be taken without the written agreement of a director.
(b) Leave over the year end is handled as follows:
(i) days carried over must be taken by 31 March;
(ii) days not taken by that date lapse without payment.
(c) Teams must agree cover for client work before leave starts.
Peak periods

Quarter-end and the two weeks before a major client deadline are treated as peak periods. During a peak period no more than one person from each team may be on leave at the same time. Directors publish the peak calendar in November for the following year, and requests made before then are accepted on a first come, first served basis.
Leaving the company
On the last day of employment, any untaken leave is paid at the normal daily rate. If you have taken more leave than you have earned, the difference is deducted from your final pay.

4.3 Sickness absence
If you are unwell you must tell your line manager before your normal starting time on the first day of absence. Sick pay is paid in full for the first 26 weeks in any rolling twelve months.
Telephone your line manager; a message left with a colleague is not enough.
Keep the manager informed every three days if the absence continues.
Send a medical note to HR from the eighth calendar day.
Return-to-work conversations are held after every period of absence of five days or more.
